shorts.title: What you will learn: if and else
shorts.hook: Your program can choose between two paths.
shorts.script: Your program can choose between two paths. Today your program learns to decide. It tests a condition, and then it takes one of two paths. An if statement tests a condition. If the condition is true, the body runs. If it is false, the body is skipped. Add an else branch for the false case. Exactly one branch runs. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: if and else.

shorts.title: if and else in one minute
shorts.hook: An if statement tests a condition.
shorts.script: An if statement tests a condition. If the condition is true, the body runs. If it is false, the body is skipped. Add an else branch for the false case. Exactly one branch runs. Think of a fork in the road. A sign says which way to walk, and you never take both paths. Marks is seventy-two. The if tests whether marks is at least thirty-five. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: if and else in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.script: Cin reads a number. An even number has remainder zero when we divide by two. That branch prints even. Seven has remainder one, so the else branch runs. The program prints seven is odd. Type seven and press Enter. The program prints seven is odd. An if statement tests a condition. The body runs only when the test is true. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: A semicolon after the if
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in if and else?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in if and else? Bug of the Day. A semicolon sits after the if test. C plus plus reads it as an empty body. The block below then always runs. With marks equal to twenty, the program would still print Pass. The compiler warns about an empty body. Remove the semicolon. A semicolon after the test is an empty body. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: A semicolon after the if.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Can you decide if a number is positive in if and else?
shorts.script: Can you decide if a number is positive in if and else? Why did the if statement break up with else? It said, you are always my second choice. Read a number. Print positive if it is greater than zero, and not positive in all other cases. Write your answer in the comments. An if statement tests a condition. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
